title: Philippine Indigenous Arts, Motifs, Textiles & Traditional Crafts
subject: Arts Appreciation
description: Manunggul Jar, Spanish colonial shift, characteristics of indigenous arts, motifs, T'nalak, Dagmay, Inaul, Pis Syabit, and traditional crafts (basketry, pottery, woodcarving, beadwork, weaving).
sourceFile: Philippine Indigenous Arts and Traditional Crafts (1).pdf, PHILIPPINE INDIGENOUS ARTS AND TRADITIONAL CRAFTS (2).pdf, ART APPRECIATION REVIEWER - FINAL EXAMINATION.pdf

questions.question: The Manunggul Jar, an archaeological burial jar discovered in Palawan, features two human figures aboard a boat on its lid. What does this motif symbolize?
options: The journey of the soul to the afterlife
questions.answer: The journey of the soul to the afterlife
questions.explanation: The boatman and passenger on the Manunggul Jar lid symbolize the soul's passage to the afterlife.

questions.question: How did the Spanish colonial period most significantly reshape Philippine visual arts and architecture?
options: It replaced all woodcarving with abstract digital installations.
Roman Catholicism shaped religious paintings, santos sculptures, and church architecture.
It introduced Japanese ukiyo-e woodblock printing across Mindanao.
It prohibited all stone and masonry construction.
questions.answer: Roman Catholicism shaped religious paintings, santos sculptures, and church architecture.
questions.explanation: Spanish colonization introduced Roman Catholic religious imagery, santos, retablos, and colonial churches.

questions.question: Which five core characteristics define Philippine Indigenous Arts?
options: Commercial branding, mass factory output, plastic media, individual isolation, purely decorative
Cultural significance, traditional knowledge, connection to nature, symbolism, and practical + artistic functions
Industrial speed, Western oil techniques, digital filters, abstract minimalism, uniformity
Uniform national rules, royal patronage, imported marble, non-functional luxury, anonymity
questions.answer: Cultural significance, traditional knowledge, connection to nature, symbolism, and practical + artistic functions
questions.explanation: Indigenous arts unite community identity, intergenerational knowledge, natural local materials, symbolism, and both practical and aesthetic functions.

questions.question: What is an 'indigenous motif'?
options: A recurring visual element, pattern, shape, or design used in a particular Indigenous community's artistic traditions
A government copyright stamp on exported crafts
A modern software plugin for 3D modeling
questions.answer: A recurring visual element, pattern, shape, or design used in a particular Indigenous community's artistic traditions
questions.explanation: Indigenous motifs include geometric patterns, nature-inspired forms, repeated/symmetrical designs, and culturally grounded symbols.

questions.question: Why should students avoid guessing the meaning of an indigenous motif without reliable cultural context?
options: Because motifs have no meaning at all
Because the same shape or symbol can carry distinct meanings in different Indigenous communities
Because motifs are strictly random accidents
Because only Western museum curators invent motif meanings
questions.answer: Because the same shape or symbol can carry distinct meanings in different Indigenous communities
questions.explanation: Interpretations must be grounded in the specific cultural knowledge of the community that creates and maintains the tradition.

questions.question: Which four visual features commonly characterize indigenous motifs?
options: Oil impasto, chiaroscuro, linear perspective, pastel Rococo
Geometric patterns, nature-inspired designs, repetition & symmetry, and symbolic designs
Neon signage, digital pixels, graffiti tags, photographic collages
Monochrome concrete, flying buttresses, pointed arches, stained glass
questions.answer: Geometric patterns, nature-inspired designs, repetition & symmetry, and symbolic designs
questions.explanation: Indigenous motifs feature diamonds/zigzags (geometric), plants/animals (nature-inspired), repetition/symmetry (rhythm/balance/unity), and ancestral symbolism.

questions.question: T'nalak is a traditional abaca textile associated with which Indigenous community and region?
options: T'boli of Lake Sebu, South Cotabato, Mindanao
questions.answer: T'boli of Lake Sebu, South Cotabato, Mindanao
questions.explanation: T'nalak is woven by the T'boli people of Lake Sebu, South Cotabato.

questions.question: Why is T'nalak called a 'dream cloth,' and who is the spirit of abaca associated with its patterns?
options: Weavers buy designs from dream catalogs; Sarimanok
Patterns are believed to be revealed to weavers in dreams connected to Fu Dalu, the spirit of abaca
It is only worn while sleeping; Bulul
The dye glows in the dark; Naga
questions.answer: Patterns are believed to be revealed to weavers in dreams connected to Fu Dalu, the spirit of abaca
questions.explanation: T'boli dreamweavers receive patterns through dreams linked to Fu Dalu, guardian spirit of abaca.

questions.question: What are the three steps of the 'warp ikat' resist-dyeing technique used in T'nalak weaving?
options: Carve, mold, and fire in a kiln
Tie selected sections of threads, dye the threads (tied parts resist dye), then weave on the loom
Bleach finished cloth, paint with oil, then lacquer
Cut geometric squares, sew together, then press with gold
questions.answer: Tie selected sections of threads, dye the threads (tied parts resist dye), then weave on the loom
questions.explanation: Warp ikat resists dye by tying specific sections of lengthwise warp threads before dyeing and weaving.

questions.question: Which traditional color palette characterizes authentic T'nalak cloth?
options: Neon pink, lime green, and silver
Red, black, and natural off-white earthy tones
Cobalt blue and bright yellow only
questions.answer: Red, black, and natural off-white earthy tones
questions.explanation: T'nalak features intricate, often symmetrical designs in red, black, and natural off-white abaca tones.

questions.question: Dagmay is an abaca tie-dye (ikat) textile associated with which community, and what distinctive motifs does it often feature?
options: Mandaya of eastern Mindanao / Davao Region; stylized human figures and crocodile forms
questions.answer: Mandaya of eastern Mindanao / Davao Region; stylized human figures and crocodile forms
questions.explanation: Mandaya Dagmay uses abaca fiber and ikat tie-dye techniques featuring stylized human figures and crocodile motifs.

questions.question: Which Mindanao textile is woven by the Maguindanaon using cotton, rayon, or lustrous specialty threads on a handloom, often worn as a tubular garment called a 'malong'?
questions.answer: Inaul
questions.explanation: Inaul is a vibrant Maguindanaon handloom-woven fabric featuring plaid and geometric designs, traditionally used for the malong.

questions.question: What types of looms are traditionally used to weave Maguindanaon Inaul?
options: Handlooms such as the backstrap loom or fixed horizontal-frame loom
questions.answer: Handlooms such as the backstrap loom or fixed horizontal-frame loom
questions.explanation: Inaul is handloom-woven—operated by hand using a backstrap or fixed horizontal-frame loom.

questions.question: Pis Syabit is a square-shaped textile with intricate, vivid geometric patterns traditionally used as a headcloth by the:
options: Tausug people of the Sulu Archipelago
questions.answer: Tausug people of the Sulu Archipelago
questions.explanation: Pis Syabit is a hallmark of Tausug weaving heritage, showcasing geometric abstraction, symmetry, and rhythm.

questions.question: Which pairing of Philippine textile and cultural community is INCORRECT?
questions.answer: Pis Syabit — Ilocano
questions.explanation: Pis Syabit belongs to the Tausug of the Sulu Archipelago; Ilocano weaving is known for abel/inabel (such as binakol).

questions.question: Which materials are commonly interlaced in traditional Philippine basketry?
questions.answer: Bamboo, rattan, buri, and pandan
questions.explanation: Basketry weaves plant strips like bamboo, rattan, buri, and pandan into functional and decorative baskets, hats, and containers.

questions.question: How do traditional crafts like basketry demonstrate both practical and artistic functions?
options: A basket can carry and store crops while displaying intricate geometric patterns with cultural meaning.
Baskets are purely sculptures that cannot hold anything.
Baskets are made exclusively for museum display cases.
Baskets have no pattern or rhythm.
questions.answer: A basket can carry and store crops while displaying intricate geometric patterns with cultural meaning.
questions.explanation: Traditional crafts blend everyday utility (carrying crops, storing rice) with aesthetic design (line, pattern, texture, rhythm).

questions.question: Pottery creates durable vessels, jars, and cooking pots by:
options: Shaping clay and firing it at high temperatures
questions.answer: Shaping clay and firing it at high temperatures
questions.explanation: Pottery combines clay, water, and natural pigments/minerals, shaped by hand and hardened with heat.

questions.question: The Ifugao 'bulul'—a carved wooden figure associated with rice rituals and community beliefs—is an example of which craft?
questions.answer: Woodcarving
questions.explanation: Philippine woodcarving transforms woods like narra, molave, acacia, and mahogany into ritual, decorative, and architectural pieces such as the Ifugao bulul.

questions.question: Which local hardwoods are commonly used in Philippine traditional woodcarving?
questions.answer: Narra, molave, acacia, and mahogany
questions.explanation: Traditional Filipino woodcarvers work with durable local woods including narra, molave, acacia, and mahogany.

questions.question: Beadwork and jewelry making in Philippine cultural communities use glass beads, wooden beads, shells, seeds, stones, and metal primarily to express:
options: Identity, social status, personal adornment, and ceremonial significance
questions.answer: Identity, social status, personal adornment, and ceremonial significance
questions.explanation: Traditional beadwork and ornaments communicate identity, status, and cultural heritage during celebrations and rituals.

questions.question: Which natural fibers are commonly used across Philippine textile weaving traditions?
questions.answer: Cotton, abaca, piña, and silk
questions.explanation: Filipino weavers use cotton, abaca, piña, silk, and specialty threads depending on the regional tradition.

questions.question: In traditional crafts, how is the element of LINE primarily expressed?
options: Through threads, stripes, carved lines, and borders
Through firing clay at high heat
Through the weight of a wooden statue
Through the smell of natural plant dyes
questions.answer: Through threads, stripes, carved lines, and borders
questions.explanation: Threads, woven stripes, incised lines, and borders all manifest the element of line in traditional crafts.

questions.question: Roughness of woven abaca, smoothness of glazed pottery, or softness of cotton fabric illustrates which element of art in crafts?
questions.answer: Texture
questions.explanation: Texture refers to the tactile surface quality—rough, smooth, thick, or soft—of craft materials.

questions.question: When repeated motifs, colors, and woven structures lead the viewer's eye smoothly across a textile or basket, which principle of art is demonstrated?
questions.answer: Rhythm
questions.explanation: Repetition of lines, colors, and shapes creates visual rhythm across woven and crafted surfaces.

questions.question: When an elder teaches traditional weaving or basketry to younger members of the community, what is taking place?
options: Preservation and intergenerational transmission of cultural knowledge
questions.answer: Preservation and intergenerational transmission of cultural knowledge
questions.explanation: Passing craft skills from elders to youth keeps cultural identity, techniques, and community history alive.

questions.question: Which textile is paired with its correct distinctive technique and feature?
options: T'nalak — warp ikat resist-dyeing on abaca with dream-inspired motifs
Inaul — clay firing at high temperatures
Pis Syabit — wooden rice god carving
questions.answer: T'nalak — warp ikat resist-dyeing on abaca with dream-inspired motifs
questions.explanation: T'nalak uses warp ikat on abaca; Inaul uses handlooms; Pis Syabit is Tausug geometric weaving; Dagmay is Mandaya abaca tie-dye weaving.

questions.question: Why is an indigenous artwork's cultural meaning NOT determined solely by its commercial price or resemblance to foreign art?
options: Because it is rooted in ancestral stories, spiritual beliefs, environment, and community practices
Because indigenous artworks cannot be sold
Because all indigenous artworks look identical
Because indigenous artworks contain no visual elements
questions.answer: Because it is rooted in ancestral stories, spiritual beliefs, environment, and community practices
questions.explanation: Indigenous art derives its deepest meaning from the community's history, beliefs, and lived traditions.

questions.question: Which craft shapes and forms metal (such as brass, silver, or bronze) into useful, ceremonial, or decorative objects?
questions.answer: Metalworking
questions.explanation: Metalworking shapes metal into tools, brassware, trays, musical instruments, and religious/decorative objects.

questions.question: How does 'unity' appear in a traditional woven textile like Pis Syabit or Inaul?
options: The different colors, geometric shapes, and patterns work together cohesively as one composition
Each corner uses an unrelated clashing fabric glued together
The cloth has no discernible pattern or border
Only a single unpainted thread is used
questions.answer: The different colors, geometric shapes, and patterns work together cohesively as one composition
questions.explanation: Unity is achieved when varied colors, shapes, and repeated motifs harmonize into an integrated whole.
